author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Francisco Partners and KKR have agreed to buy minority stakes in Italian software company TeamSystem from Hellman & Friedman, Reuters reported Friday, citing people familiar with the private transaction. Francisco Partners is set to acquire about 10%, while KKR and other investors would purchase roughly another 5%.

The deal values TeamSystem at between €8 billion and €10 billion, according to the sources. TeamSystem provides accounting, payroll and business-management software to companies and professionals. Its products are closely connected to government electronic-invoicing systems used by small and midsize businesses, a position investors see as difficult for new AI-driven competitors to reproduce quickly.

The transaction is notable after concerns about artificial intelligence contributed to a sharp selloff in software stocks and complicated private-equity exits. It lets Hellman & Friedman return some capital while moving its remaining holding to another fund under its management. The firms and TeamSystem declined to comment to Reuters. Because the terms were described by unnamed sources and the deal was not accompanied by a public closing announcement, final ownership details could still change.
dek: Sources say the private transaction values the Italian business-software provider at between €8 billion and €10 billion.
headline: KKR and Francisco Partners take minority stakes in TeamSystem
